therapeutic

thair-uh-PYOO-tik -- stress on the third syllable, PYOO. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Therapeutic is healing or corrective; helping to restore health or well-being.

The hospital offers therapeutic music sessions that ease patients' pain and lower their stress.

Example

After the wildfire, counselors set up daily art sessions where children paint what they saw, and week by week the drawings -- and the children -- grow calmer.

The art sessions are therapeutic: they actively help the children heal. Therapeutic covers whatever restores health or well-being, whether the healing is physical, emotional, or both.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

healing: Healing describes whatever mends the body or mind -- a healing wound is closing, and a healing balm helps it close. Therapeutic frames that same help as treatment: a therapeutic exercise or dose is chosen on purpose, as part of care meant to restore health.

comforting: Comforting means easing someone's distress right now -- a comforting hug or word makes the next few minutes easier, and the claim ends when the moment does. Therapeutic reaches further: a therapeutic habit or treatment actually helps you heal, restoring well-being in a way that lasts.

medicinal: Medicinal means working like a medicine -- a medicinal herb contains something that treats the body. It stays physical and drug-like. Therapeutic is wider: therapeutic care can work through music, art, or exercise, restoring well-being of mind as well as body.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

harmful: causing damage or injury

injurious: causing harm, especially to health

Where it sits · how big a health claim it makes — restorative → therapeutic → curative

restorative vs. therapeutic: Restorative is the gentler claim -- a restorative nap gives back energy, while calling something therapeutic suggests it genuinely helps heal a real hurt, whether in the body or the mind.

curative vs. therapeutic: Curative makes a stronger promise than therapeutic: a therapeutic treatment helps you heal and feel better, while a curative one claims to eliminate the illness itself, start to finish.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — therapeut-

Root — therapeut-: one who treats or cares for (from Greek therapeuein, 'to treat medically, take care of'; therapeutes, 'attendant, healer')

Suffix — -ic

Suffix — -ic: having the characteristics of; like (Greek -ikos, via Latin -icus)

Put it together

Put it together: Therapeutic builds on Greek therapeuein, 'to treat medically, to take care of': therapeut- (from therapeutes, 'one who treats or attends') + -ic ('having the characteristics of'). Something therapeutic has the character of treatment and care -- it works to heal, correct, and restore, the same root that gives us therapy itself.

Use the root in a new word: therapist

Use the root in a new word: therapist: After the accident, a physical therapist helped him regain full movement in his knee.

Root Check

Word Choice

Therapeutic works at two volumes: the strict medical sense (a therapeutic dose, therapeutic exercises) and the everyday sense for anything that soothes and restores ('I find folding laundry oddly therapeutic'). Both flow from the same idea -- treatment and care that heal.
